ios.desc:
Toned does not apply a film look. It runs the photochemistry: your photo is exposed onto an emulsion, developed, printed through an enlarger onto photographic paper, and toned.

The negative is a real step, not a figure of speech. You can look at it, orange mask and all, and export it, before you make a print from it.

HOW IT WORKS
Every stage is a stage, in order, and each one takes its input from the one before it.
- Load a film. Every stock has its own characteristic curve, one per dye layer, which is why changing the exposure does not do the same thing on every stock.
- Expose it. Stops, not a brightness slider.
- Develop it. Push and pull move contrast, grain and shadow density the way development time does, and the app says what it did.
- Look at the negative. The orange integral dye mask on the color stocks, clear base on the black and white ones.
- Print it. Enlarger exposure, paper grade 0 to 5 in half steps, and the paper's own response curve and maximum black.
- Dodge and burn. Light held back or given, in stops, before the paper's curve. That is why burning a blown sky brings tone back instead of turning white into grey.
- Tone the print. Toners work by density, so they reach the shadows or the midtones first, the way the chemistry does.

WHY IT LOOKS LIKE THIS
- Halation happens where the emulsion was blown through to the antihalation layer, and it bleeds into the red-sensitive layer. On the tungsten motion picture stock, which has that layer stripped off, every bright light wears a red halo.
- Grain lives in the density. It is coarsest through the mid tones and thins out in the deep shadows and the blown highlights, because that is where the crystals are.
- The orange mask is not a color wash. It is base density, and the enlarger's color head cancels it at print time.
- Paper is not a filter. A glossy fiber base holds a deeper black than a matte, and the matte has no true black at all.

THE SHELF
- Thirteen film stocks: nine color negative, four black and white, from almost grainless to grain the size of the subject.
- Five papers: resin coated and fiber base, neutral, warmtone and matte.
- Four toners: selenium, sepia, gold and copper.
- Split-grade printing: a soft exposure at grade 0 for the highlights and a hard one at grade 5 for the blacks, timed separately.

LOOKING AT IT
- Hold the compare button to see the photograph you started with, at any point in the chain.
- Pinch to magnify the print. The grain is really there: it is re-rendere

quotes.text:
I am interested in simulating pyshical processes in software so i decided to build an iPhone app that simulates film negatives and paper.

It models in 2 stages:
scene light -> color negative -> print reflectance

The negative uses per-dye-layer H&D curves and the paper also has its own response curves.

If you've ever spent time in a real darkroom, I would really like you to try the app and share your opinions.

App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6799706160
